notes.text: Prayed — That is, praised God; which is a part of prayer. Rejoiceth - Or, leapeth for joy: for the words note not only inward joy, but also the outward demonstrations of it. In the Lord - As the author of my joy, that he hath heard my prayer, and accepted my son for his service. Horn - My strength and glory (which are often signified by an horn,) are advanced and manifested to my vindication, and the confusion of mine enemies. Mouth enlarged - That is, opened wide to pour forth abundant praises to God, and to give a full answer to all the reproaches of mine adversaries. Enemies - So she manifests her prudence and modesty, in not naming Peninnah, but only her enemies in the general. Salvation - Because the matter of my joy is no trivial thing, but that strange and glorious salvation or deliverance which thou hast given me from my oppressing care and grief, and from the insolencies and reproaches of mine enemies.

None holy — None so perfectly, unchangeably and constantly holy. None beside - Not only none is so holy as thou art, but in truth there is none holy besides thee; namely, entirely, or independently, but only by participation from thee. Any rock - Thou only art a sure defense and refuge to all that flee to thee.

Talk no more — Thou Peninnah, boast no more of thy numerous off-spring, and speak no more insolently and scornfully of me. She speaks of her in the plural number, because she would not expose her name to censure. Of knowledge - He knoweth thy heart, and all that pride, and envy, and contempt of me, which thy own conscience knows; and all thy perverse carriage towards me. Actions - That is, he trieth all mens thoughts and actions, (for the Hebrew word signifies both) as a just judge, to give to every one according to their works.
Bows — The strength of which they boasted. Stumbled - Or, were weak, or feeble, in body and spirit.

Hired themselves out for bread — It is the same thing which is expressed both in divers metaphors in the foregoing, and following verses. Ceased - That is, ceased to be hungry. Seven - That is, many, as seven is often used. She speaks in the prophetick style, the past time, for the future; for though she had actually born but one, yet she had a confident persuasion that she should have more, which was grounded either upon some particular assurance from God; or rather upon the prayer or prediction of Eli. She - That is, Peninnah. Feeble - Either because she was now past child-bearing: or, because divers of her children, which were her strength and her glory, were dead, as the Hebrew doctors relate.

Killeth — The same person whom he first killeth, or bringeth nigh unto death, he afterwards raiseth to life. Me, who was almost consumed with grief, he hath revived. The name of death both in sacred scripture, and profane writers, is often given to great Calamities.

From the dunghill — From the most sordid place, and mean estate. Inherit - Not only possess it themselves, but transmit it to their posterity. Throne - That is, a glorious throne or kingdom. Pillars - The foundations of the earth, which God created, and upholds, and wherewith he sustains the earth, and all its inhabitants, as a house is supported with pillars; and therefore it is not strange if he disposeth of persons and things therein as he pleaseth.

Feet — That is, the steps or paths, their counsels and actions; he will keep; that is, both uphold, that they may not fall into ruin; and direct and preserve from wandering, and from those fatal errors that wicked men daily run into. Silent - Shall be put to silence: they who used to open their mouths wide against heaven, and against the saints, shall be so confounded with the unexpected disappointment of all their hopes, and with God's glorious appearance and operations for his people, that they shall have their mouths quite stopped. Darkness - Both inward, in their own minds, not knowing what to say or do; and outward, in a stat e of deep distress. Prevail - Namely, against God, or against his saints, as the wicked were confident they should do, because of their great power, and wealth, and numbers.

Exalt — Increase, or advance the strength. Of his anointed - Of his king. This may respect Christ, the singular anointed one of God, and the special king of his people. In this sense also, the Lord shall judge the ends of the earth: David's victories and dominions reached far. But God will give to the Son of David, the uttermost parts of the earth for his possession. And he will give strength unto his king, for the accomplishing his great undertaking, and exalt the horn, of the power and honour of his anointed, till he hath put all his enemies under his feet.

glossa.text:
*It is enlarged. ((RAB.))* Because the word of God is not bound in tribulations, not bound in its heralds.

((ID.)) Unto Christ, whom the aged Simeon embraces as a child and knows to be great, saying: *Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord, according to thy word, in peace. Because my eyes have seen thy salvation ((Luc. II))*. If I shall have rejoiced in the salvation of God, then shall my mouth be enlarged. Namely, through meditation upon the word of God one comes to the lifting up of the heart, whence: *Our mouth is open to you, O Corinthians, our heart is enlarged ((II Cor. V))*. Out of the breadth of the heart wisdom is ministered to the mouth.

*There is none holy.* ((RAB.)) Beside thee, O Lord, because none is made holy save by thee, and though there be those that are called many gods and many lords, yet none of them is by nature that which God is; because he alone is he who saith: *I am who am ((Exod. III))*. For a shadow, in comparison with a body, is not, nor smoke in comparison with fire.

*As the Lord is. ((ID.))* He saith not, save the Lord: *But none is as the Lord,* holy and sanctifying, just and justifying.

*Multiply not to speak lofty things, glorying.* He reproves the Jews and the wise of the world, who exalt themselves against the knowledge of God. Solomon: *Seek not the things that are too high for thee,* and elsewhere: *God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: let thy words be few.*

*Old things,* etc. Which pertain to the old man, that is, to carnal converse, seek ye knowledge, which is not save from God: because he himself is the Lord of knowledges, in whom are all the treasures of wisdom.

*Unto him thoughts are prepared.* Because he withdraws himself from thoughts which are without understanding, or thoughts are prepared for him, that is, are made manifest. Whence: *The Lord knoweth the thoughts of men.*

*The God of knowledges. ((RAB., ubi supra.))* He himself knoweth you, etc., *as far as* and they are not from him from whom men are.

((RAB.)) That is, the intention of those who seem to themselves to be mighty, so that without God's help they may be able to fulfil the divine commandments.

*And the weak.* ((RAB.)) They who trust in the goodness of God say: *Have mercy on me, O God, for I am weak ((Psal. VI))*. Weak was the Gentile people, when it was estranged from the testament of God, but now, girt about with strength, when it is clothed with the shield of faith and the helmet of salvation and the sword of the spirit, it will be able to quench the fiery darts of the devil.

*They that were filled before hired themselves out for bread.* The Jews, filled before, namely with the mysteries of the oracles, hired themselves out for bread, that is, they separated themselves from God: or they tore themselves away from their own seats, lest they should receive the Gospel that treats of the bread which came down from heaven. Filled were those same who were also the mighty, that is, the Israelites to whom the oracles of God were entrusted, but sons of the bondwoman, were made less, who withdrew themselves and believed not in the Saviour, and in those very loaves, that is, in the divine oracles, savoured only earthly things. But the nations, to whom the law was not given, after through the New Testament they came to those oracles, passed over the earth by much hungering, because in them they savoured not earthly but heavenly things. In the Greek thus: *They that were full of bread were made less, and they that were hungry passed over the earth.*

*And the hungry.* That is, the Gentiles, before in want, now taste the bread of the word of God, since it is sweet. So long have they been fed with the knowledge of God.

*The barren hath borne.* In the number seven the universality of the Church is designated, whence John also writes to seven churches, showing that he writes to the fulness of one; whence: *Wisdom hath built herself a house, and hath propped up seven pillars ((Prov. IX))*. Barren was the Church among the nations, before this offspring which we behold arose. We behold too the earthly Jerusalem fruitful, now made weak: because whosoever were free sons in her were of her strength: but now, since the letter is there, the spirit is not: her strength being lost, she is made weak.

((RAB.)) *Many* in the Hebrew and in the LXX stands *seven.* The Jews say that when Samuel was born the firstborn son of Phenenna died: and that at the birth of each of Anna's sons one of Phenenna's died. But Phenenna had seven: and Anna five. Yet the Hebrews reckon the two sons of Samuel among the sons of Anna.

((ID.)) The barren woman, etc., *as far as* by this his poverty we have been enriched.
*The poor,* etc. Jesus, who for our sakes was made poor, and the Lord enriches the same with the glory of the resurrection.

*Out of the dust.* Christ out of corruption, whence: *Nor wilt thou give thy holy one to see corruption ((Psal. XV))*.

 *Out of the dunghill. ((RAB., ubi supra.))* Out of the Jewish people, in which, when the Apostle had said that he had persecuted the Church, *the things,* saith he, *that were gain to me, those I have counted for Christ dung [detrimenta] ((Philip. III))*.

*With princes.* ((ID.)) To whom it is said: *You shall sit upon twelve seats, judging the twelve tribes of Israel ((Matth. XXV))*.

*The throne of glory.* By sitting in the equity of the Father, and because *the Father hath given all judgment to the Son, and because of his kingdom there shall be no end ((Joan. V))*.

*The poles of the earth.* Namely the four quarters of the world, in which he has enlarged the globe of the Church, which *from the rising of the sun unto the going down praise the name of the Lord ((Psal. CXII))*. 

Mystically, the preachers, upon whom the globe, that is, the Church, is made firm by their faith, of whom it is said: *Under whom they stoop that bear up the world ((Job. IX))*.

*They shall fear the Lord.* Because he will make his adversary weak. It can also be understood, from the ambiguous Greek, as his own adversary. For when the Lord begins to possess us, our adversary becomes his own; and he is conquered by us, not by our strength, because a man is not mighty in his own power. *They shall fear the Lord.* The Jews, his adversaries, over whom the Lord thundered in the heavens, that is, in the apostles, when he terrified them by threatening hell, confirming his threats by signs: whence many were converted. Or they shall fear in the judgment him whom here, opposing him, they despised, over whom he will thunder, saying: *Go into everlasting fire ((Matth. XXV))*. And lest this befall all, the Lord thunders daily in the heavens, that is, in the Scriptures and the doctors.

*In the heavens.* ((RAB.)) Because the just retribution is to come in the day of judgment, but meanwhile he thunders out of his clouds, which he filled with the Holy Spirit after he ascended the heavens.

*The ends.* The last things of a man: because those things will not be judged which in the meantime are changed for the better or for the worse, but the last things in which he shall have been found.

*And he will give.* That is, to Christ

*Dominion.* That is, the Church, whence: *I will give thee the nations for thine inheritance.* Or dominion, that is, the power of judging, because *he hath given all judgment to the Son.*

*To his king.* ((RAB.)) To the Christian people, to whom he gives strength to rule the flesh, that in it he may overcome the world, who for its sake shed his own blood.

 *Of his Christ. ((RAB., in lib. Reg. ))* Of the Christian people, anointed with chrism: yet the whole body with its head is one Christ. These things Anna the mother of Samuel prophesied, in whom the change of the old priesthood was then figured, and now fulfilled, when the fruitful woman was made weak, that the barren might have a new priesthood in Christ.

notes.text: Humbleth — Who is so high, that it is a wonderful condescention in him to take any notice of his heavenly host, and much more of sinful and miserable men upon earth.

Princes — As he did Joseph, David, and others. His people - Who in God's account are far more honourable than the princes of Heathen nations. This and the four following psalms, the Jews were wont to sing at the close of the paschal supper. It is a solemn commemoration of God's delivering Israel, giving them the law, and water out of the rock, ver. 1-8.

glossa.text: *Praise ye.* ((ID.)) First the Prophet admonishes the devout to praise continually, and everywhere to preach. Secondly he himself does what he admonishes others to do, that is, he praises God there: *Who is as the Lord ((I Cor. XIV))*? Admonishing therefore unto praise, he shows and says who and whom, and how long, and where, and why they should praise. *Children.* Not in sense, but in malice, and chiefly in pride, that is, the humble; whence, *Be not children in sense, but in malice be children, that in mind ye may be perfect.* ((AUG., CASS.)) Praise the Lord, ye children, the simple and the pure, who ought to praise.

*Let the name be.* ((CASS.)) Behold, he has said who and whom they ought to praise; then he subjoins how long we praise *laudamus*; read *laudandus*, "is to be praised", namely always. *Let the name of the Lord be:* lest ye think that I command praise for an hour, etc., *as far as* by the Gentiles the carnal, by the heavens the spiritual.
*From the rising of the sun.* ((AUG.)) Here he says that he ought to be praised everywhere.
*Above the heavens.* ((ID.)) The Apostles, through whom he reigns among the Gentiles, and is; therefore I invite to praises, because he is to reign above all.

*Who is as.* ((CASS.)) Secondly he himself does what he admonishes others to do, that by the deed also he may teach others. *Who?* None that can of himself. *In the high places,* etc. In the angels and the saints: and although he is high, he despises not the lowly.

*The lowly things.* These are they who by his gift are made high, and in them he sits. *He beholdeth,* the lowly one by one. *In the earth,* the saints, whom he so beholds as, on the contrary, he hates the proud.
*Raising up from the earth:* from the labour of the body. *Out of the dunghill,* he is lifted up over whom the vices of the flesh have no dominion.

*Who maketh to dwell.* ((CASS., AUG.)) He expounds where he raises up and lifts up, etc., *as far as* out of the mammon of iniquity by works of mercy. *The barren woman.* ((AUG.)) Namely Sara, that is, the Gentile Church, which was barren before, whereby she is signified by Sara. Her, I say, he makes to dwell in the house, that is, in the Church of the Jews, among the Jews themselves, that in the corner-stone the two walls may be joined together, and there may be made one fold. *Of children.* ((ID.)) In whose person these things are said, etc., *as far as* since I know myself to be without children, and a widow.

notes.text: Having spoken of faith and its fruit, ver. 3, &c., he comes now to love. The ninth, tenth, and eleventh verses refer to chapter the seventh; the twelfth verse to chapter the eighth; the thirteenth verse, of communicating to the saints, whether Jews or gentiles, to chapter the ninth, &c. Part of the sixteenth verse is repeated from chap. xi, 25. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good — Both inwardly and outwardly, whatever ill-will or danger may follow.
In honour preferring one another — Which you will do, if you habitually consider what is good in others, and what is evil in yourselves.
Whatsoever ye do, do it with your might. In every business diligently and fervently serving the Lord — Doing all to God, not to man.

Rejoicing in hope — Of perfect holiness and everlasting happiness. Hitherto of faith and love; now of hope also, see the fifth and eighth chapters; afterwards of duties toward others; saints, ver. 13 persecutors, ver. 14 friends, strangers, enemies, ver. 15, &c.

Communicate to the necessities of the saints — Relieve all Christians that are in want. It is remarkable, that the apostle, treating expressly of the duties flowing from the communion of saints, yet never says one word about the dead. Pursue hospitality - Not only embracing those that offer, but seeking opportunities to exercise it.
Curse not — No, not in your heart.
Rejoice — The direct opposite to weeping is laughter; but this does not so well suit a Christian.
Mind not high things — Desire not riches, honour, or the company of the great.

glossa.text:
*Not slothful.* Cursed is he that does the work of God negligently; the slothful man is without hope in the divine converse. And therefore, that the cold of sloth may be driven off, *Be ye fervent,* etc.

*Fervent in spirit. ((THEOD.))* He called grace the Spirit, etc., *as far as* for this he said. *Instant in prayer.* That is, doing this assiduously.

*Serving the Lord,* etc. As if he should say: Although I have said that ye should be fervent in spirit, yet do not thrust in the words of God everywhere and unseasonably, but be fervent with the opportunity of the time, so that ye may speak the words of faith in fit places, to fit persons, and at a fit time. *Fervent.* The Spirit is fire, with which charity is fervent, whence the Lord says: *I am come to send fire on the earth, and what will I, but that it burn? ((Luc. XII.))*
*Rejoicing in hope.* Being certain of things to come they rejoice, and therefore are patient in tribulation.

*Consenting.* Which is not done with the mouth only, because then is there true humility, if it is not in the tongue alone, lest, presuming upon themselves, they should not suffer with others, but reproach them.

notes.text: A city of Judah — Probably Hebron, which was situated in the hill country of Judea, and belonged to the house of Aaron.

When Elisabeth heard the salutation of Mary — The discourse with which she saluted her, giving an account of what the angel had said, the joy of her soul so affected her body, that the very child in her womb was moved in an uncommon manner, as if it leaped for joy.
Happy is she that believed — Probably she had in her mind the unbelief of Zacharias.
And Mary said — Under a prophetic impulse, several things, which perhaps she herself did not then fully understand.

My spirit hath rejoiced in God my saviour — She seems to turn her thoughts here to Christ himself, who was to be born of her, as the angel had told her, he should be the Son of the Highest, whose name should be Jesus, the saviour. And she rejoiced in hope of salvation through faith in him, which is a blessing common to all true believers, more than in being his mother after the flesh, which was an honour peculiar to her. And certainly she had the same reason to rejoice in God her saviour hat we have: because he had regarded the low estate of his handmaid, in like manner as he regarded our low estate; and vouchsafed to come and save her and us, when we were reduced to the lowest estate of sin and misery.

He hath wrought strength with his arm — That is, he hath shown the exceeding greatness of his power. She speaks prophetically of those things as already done, which God was about to do by the Messiah. He hath scattered the proud - Visible and invisible.
He hath put down the mighty — Both angels and men.
He hath helped his servant Israel — By sending the Messiah.
To his seed — His spiritual seed: all true believers.
Mary returned to her own house — And thence soon after to Bethlehem.

glossa.text: *And Mary rising up in those days, went into the hill country with haste into a city of Juda. ((AMBR.))* Not incredulous of the oracle, etc., *as far as* when it is added: *And it came to pass, that when she heard.*

*And she entered into the house of Zachary.* From this let holy women learn what attentiveness they ought to show to kinswomen with child.

*And saluted Elizabeth. ((BEDA.))* She salutes first, because it is fitting that the chaster she is, the humbler she should be.

*He exulted,* etc. Because he could not with the tongue, he salutes with an exulting spirit, and begins the office of his forerunning. Behold, there appears what the angel had said: *He shall be filled with the Holy Ghost even from his mother's womb.*

*Blessed art thou. ((BEDA, AMBR.))* The words of the Gospel agree with the words of the psalm in which it is promised to David: *Of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy throne ((Psal. CXXXI))*. And Mary is blessed by Elizabeth with the same voice as by Gabriel, so that she may be shown venerable both to angels and to men, and to be preferred before our women.
*The mother of the Lord.* I perceive the miracle, I acknowledge the mystery: the mother of the Lord, teeming with the Word, full of God.

*As was made.* In the very moment in which the voice enters the ears of the body, a spiritual power enters the heart of the hearer, and kindles not only the mother but also the offspring with love of her who comes.

*He exulted. ((BEDA.))* By the revealing of the Spirit with whom she was filled, etc., *as far as* the virgin believed where the priest denied.
*My soul doth magnify the Lord. ((ID.))* First she professes the gifts spiritually granted to her, etc., *as far as* I spend in the keeping of his commandments.

*And hath exulted. ((ID.)) ((ID.))* Because I do not care for earthly things, prosperity does not soften me, adversity does not break me, but the memory of him alone delights me, from whom eternal salvation is hoped for; I rejoice in the Godhead of him by whose conception in time my flesh is made fruitful.

*Because he hath regarded. ((ID.))* Behold how lowly are the things she feels concerning herself, etc., *as far as* and out of the small and the weak he makes them great and strong.

*Because he hath done great things to me.* Because in me he took flesh, and cleansed me from sins, and conferred upon me the gifts of the Holy Ghost.

 *And mercy. ((BEDA.))* From the special gifts she turns herself to the general judgments of God, etc., *as far as* he adds what the despisers deserve.

*He hath filled the hungry with good things. ((ID.))* They who desire eternal things with all zeal; shall be filled, when Christ shall have appeared in glory. But they who rejoice in earthly things are sent away at the last empty of all blessedness. In the present life also we see the humble filled with divine grace, and the proud deprived of the light of truth.

*As he spoke to our fathers.* Making mention of the fathers to whom this salvation was revealed, she names Abraham expressly, to whom the incarnation itself was first made manifest. *And to his seed for ever.* Not so much to those born of the flesh as to those who have followed the footsteps of faith, to whom the coming of the Saviour was promised for ever, because the promise of the inheritance itself shall be closed by no end. For both unto the end of the world believers shall not be lacking, and the glory of blessedness shall be everlasting.

*And Mary abode. ((BEDA.))* She abode so long, until she should see the nativity of the forerunner, for the sake of which above all she had come. Nor did she abide so long for the sake of familiarity alone, but that in so long a time the advancement both of Elizabeth and of John might grow. For if at Mary's first coming they were filled with the Holy Ghost, much was added to them over and above by so long a delay of her stay.

echoes.text: Vengeance is mine, and recompense, at the time when their foot slides; for the day of their calamity is at hand. Their doom rushes at them.”
echoes.note: 12:19 cites with the formula 'it is written': 'Vengeance belongs to me; I will repay, says the Lord.' The wording reflects the Song of Moses (with a form closer to the Targum/Hebrew than LXX), making divine retribution the ground for renouncing personal revenge.

echoes.text: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink: for you will heap coals of fire on his head, and Yahweh will reward you.
echoes.note: 12:20 quotes nearly verbatim: 'If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink; for in doing so you will heap coals of fire on his head.' Paul takes over the LXX wisdom saying whole as the positive counterpart to renounced vengeance.

echoes.text: “‘You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people; but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge... you shall love your neighbor' is the holiness-code substratum of the whole love-section: 'let love be without hypocrisy,' 'do not avenge yourselves,' and the love of brothers all draw on this command Paul elsewhere makes the summary of the law (13:9).

echoes.text: Hate evil, love good, and establish justice in the courts. It may be that Yahweh, the God of Armies, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.”
echoes.note: 'Abhor that which is evil; cling to that which is good' (12:9) closely renders the prophetic imperative 'Hate evil and love good'; the antithetical evil/good pairing matches Amos's covenant ethics.

echoes.text: Don’t be wise in your own eyes. Fear Yahweh, and depart from evil.
echoes.note: 'Do not be wise in your own conceits' (12:16) reproduces 'Be not wise in your own eyes' (LXX), the same proverb that grounded 12:3; here it caps the call to humble association with the lowly.

echoes.text: Don’t say, “I will pay back evil.” Wait for Yahweh, and he will save you.
echoes.note: 'Do not say, I will repay evil; wait for the LORD and he will save you' is the wisdom source for 'Repay no one evil for evil' (12:17) joined to leaving wrath to God (12:19) — the Proverb already links non-retaliation with reliance on divine vindication.

echoes.text: Depart from evil, and do good. seek peace, and pursue it.
echoes.note: 'Depart from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it' underlies both 'abhor evil... cling to good' (12:9) and 'be at peace with all men' (12:18); the twin evil-shunning and peace-pursuing maxims are reflected together.

echoes.text: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!
echoes.note: 'Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes' reinforces the prophetic condemnation of self-conceit that Paul forbids in 12:16.

echoes.text: Don’t say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will render to the man according to his work.”
echoes.note: 'Do not say, I will do to him as he has done to me; I will pay the man back for what he has done' directly parallels the prohibition of returning evil for evil in 12:17.

echoes.text: So you will find favor, and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
echoes.note: 'Respect what is honorable in the sight of all men' (12:17) echoes 'find favor and good repute in the sight of God and man' (LXX Prov 3:4), the wisdom ideal of conduct visibly good before others.

echoes.text: Be not lacking to those who weep; And mourn with those who mourn.
echoes.note: 'Do not fail those who weep, but mourn with those who mourn' is a strikingly close Second Temple parallel to 'weep with those who weep' (12:15); a wisdom maxim of empathetic solidarity rather than a quotation.

echoes.text: Yahweh, you God to whom vengeance belongs, you God to whom vengeance belongs, shine out.
echoes.note: 'O LORD, God of vengeance' confirms that retribution belongs to God alone — the theological premise of 12:19 that Paul anchors in Deuteronomy 32:35; possible secondary resonance.

echoes.text: You who love Yahweh, hate evil. He preserves the souls of his saints. He delivers them out of the hand of the wicked.
echoes.note: 'You who love the LORD, hate evil' offers a further scriptural pairing of love and abhorrence of evil behind 12:9.

echoes.text: Surely he mocks the mockers, but he gives grace to the humble.
echoes.note: 'God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble' undergirds 'associate with the humble; do not be high-minded' (12:16); the humility motif is the same wisdom orientation James and 1 Peter also draw from this verse.
echoes.lxxText: The Lord resists the proud; but he gives grace to the humble.

echoes.text: Didn’t I weep for him who was in trouble? Wasn’t my soul grieved for the needy?
echoes.note: 'Did I not weep for him whose day was hard? Was not my soul grieved for the poor?' anticipates the compassionate mourning-with-the-mourner of 12:15.

echoes.text: But as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth. I afflicted my soul with fasting. My prayer returned into my own bosom. I behaved myself as though it had been my friend or my brother. I bowed down mourning, as one who mourns his mother.
echoes.note: The psalmist's mourning and prayer for his persecutors ('I afflicted myself... I went about as one who laments for his mother') parallels both 'weep with those who weep' (12:15) and 'bless those who persecute you' (12:14).

echoes.text: The stranger who lives as a foreigner with you shall be to you as the native-born among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am Yahweh your God.
echoes.note: The command to love the resident alien 'as yourself' grounds the welcome of strangers behind 'given to hospitality' (12:13) within the same holiness-code love ethic that governs the pericope.

echoes.text: Yahweh appeared to him by the oaks of Mamre, as he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day. He lifted up his eyes and looked, and saw that three men stood opposite him. When he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself to the earth, and said, “My lord, if now I have found favor in your sight, please don’t go away from your servant. Now let a little water be fetched, wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree. I will […]
echoes.note: Abraham's hospitality to the three visitors is the paradigm narrative of welcome that informs the early-Christian virtue 'given to hospitality' (12:13).

echoes.text: The greater you are, humble yourself the more, And you will find favor before the Lord. For great is the potency of the Lord, And he is glorified of those who are lowly.
echoes.note: 'The greater you are, the more you must humble yourself... what is committed to you, attend to in humility' parallels 'do not set your mind on high things, but associate with the humble' (12:16) as Second Temple humility instruction.

echoes.text: May Yahweh judge between me and you, and may Yahweh avenge me of you; but my hand shall not be on you.
echoes.note: David's refusal to harm Saul — 'May the LORD avenge me on you, but my hand shall not be against you' — is a narrative enactment of leaving vengeance to God and not repaying evil for evil (12:17, 19).

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: The children struggled together within her. She said, “If it be so, why do I live?” She went to inquire of Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'The baby leaped in her womb' recalls the children who 'struggled (leaped) together within' Rebekah (Genesis 25:22 LXX), the one OT scene of pre-natal movement bearing prophetic significance about the elder/younger. The distinctive womb-movement motif gives high volume.

echoes.text: You shall be blessed in the fruit of your body, the fruit of your ground, the fruit of your animals, the increase of your livestock, and the young of your flock.
echoes.note: 'Blessed is the fruit of your womb' quotes the covenant blessing of Deuteronomy 28:4, 'Blessed shall be the fruit of your womb.' The exact fruit-of-the-womb-blessing formula gives high volume and casts Mary's child as the supreme covenant blessing.

echoes.text: “Jael shall be blessed above women, the wife of Heber the Kenite; blessed shall she be above women in the tent.
echoes.note: 'Blessed are you among women' repeats the Jael blessing of Judges 5:24, now on Elizabeth's lips. Recurrence (cf. 1:28) confirms this as a deliberate, sustained scriptural beatitude pattern.

echoes.text: Ozias said to her, “Blessed are you, daughter, in the sight of the Most High God, above all the women upon the earth; and blessed is the Lord God, who created the heavens and the earth, who directed you to cut off the head of the prince of our enemies.
echoes.note: Elizabeth's acclamation matches Uzziah's blessing of Judith, 'Blessed are you above all women on earth' (Judith 13:18), the nearest verbal parallel for the woman-through-whom-God-delivers beatitude. A strong deuterocanonical recurrence.

echoes.text: David was afraid of Yahweh that day; and he said, “How shall Yahweh’s ark come to me?”
echoes.note: 'Why am I so favored, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?' echoes David's awe before the ark: 'How can the ark of the Lord come to me?' (2 Samuel 6:9). With Mary's three-month stay (1:56) paralleling the ark's three months (2 Samuel 6:11), Luke figurally presents Mary as the ark of the new covenant; the reading is widely held but disputed.

echoes.text: David danced before Yahweh with all his might; and David was clothed in a linen ephod. So David and all the house of Israel brought up Yahweh’s ark with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet. It was so, as Yahweh’s ark came into the city of David, that Michal the daughter of Saul looked out at the window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before Yahweh; and she despised him in her heart.
echoes.note: 'The baby leaped in my womb for joy' echoes David's leaping and dancing for joy before the ark (2 Samuel 6:14-16). The cultic joy before the bearer of the Lord's presence supports the Mary-as-ark typology of the pericope; the link is figural and contested.

echoes.text: Hannah prayed, and said: “My heart exults in Yahweh! My horn is exalted in Yahweh. My mouth is enlarged over my enemies, because I rejoice in your salvation.
echoes.note: The Magnificat's opening, 'My soul magnifies the Lord, my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior,' is modeled directly on Hannah's Song: 'My heart exults in the Lord... I rejoice in your salvation' (1 Samuel 2:1). Hannah's hymn is the structural template for the whole canticle; high volume and strong recurrence.

echoes.text: She vowed a vow, and said, “Yahweh of Armies, if you will indeed look on the affliction of your handmaid, and remember me, and not forget your handmaid, but will give to your handmaid a boy, then I will give him to Yahweh all the days of his life, and no razor shall come on his head.”
echoes.note: 'He has looked at the humble state (tapeinosin) of his handmaid' quotes Hannah's prayer that God would 'look on the affliction (tapeinosin) of your handmaid' (1 Samuel 1:11 LXX). The shared rare-noun + handmaid combination is high-volume and ties the canticle's singer to Hannah.

echoes.text: Leah said, “Happy am I, for the daughters will call me happy.” She named him Asher.
echoes.note: 'From now on, all generations will call me blessed' takes up Leah's 'the women will call me blessed' (Genesis 30:13 LXX), spoken at the birth of a son. The call-me-blessed formula is distinctive matriarchal speech, here universalized to all generations.

echoes.text: He has sent redemption to his people. He has ordained his covenant forever. His name is holy and awesome!
echoes.note: 'Holy is his name' quotes Psalm 111:9, 'holy and awesome is his name' (cf. Psalm 99:3). The fixed liturgical predication of the divine name gives high volume; Psalm 111 also feeds the Benedictus (1:68), showing recurrence.

echoes.text: But Yahweh’s loving kindness is from everlasting to everlasting with those who fear him, his righteousness to children’s children;
echoes.note: 'His mercy is for generations of generations on those who fear him' quotes Psalm 103:17, 'the steadfast love of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear him.' The mercy + on-those-who-fear-him + perpetual-generations combination is high-volume and distinctive.

echoes.text: yet I will rejoice in Yahweh. I will be joyful in the God of my salvation!
echoes.note: 'My spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior' closely matches 'I will rejoice in the Lord; I will take joy in the God of my salvation' (Habakkuk 3:18 LXX). The rejoice-in-God-my-savior formula is distinctive and reinforces the exultant-prophetic-hymn register.

echoes.text: My soul shall be joyful in Yahweh. It shall rejoice in his salvation.
echoes.note: 'My soul shall rejoice in the Lord, exulting in his salvation' (Psalm 35:9) supplies the soul-rejoices-in-salvation diction underlying 1:47. A coherent psalmic echo within the cluster of rejoicing-in-God's-deliverance texts.

echoes.text: I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
echoes.note: 'My soul shall exult in my God' (Isaiah 61:10) within the Spirit-anointed-good-news passage contributes to the rejoicing diction of the canticle's opening. Thematic coherence with eschatological salvation supports the echo.

echoes.text: Leah conceived, and bore a son, and she named him Reuben. For she said, “Because Yahweh has looked at my affliction. For now my husband will love me.”
echoes.note: 'He has looked at the humble state' also echoes Leah's 'the Lord has looked upon my affliction' at Reuben's birth (Genesis 29:32 LXX). The look-on-affliction-of-the-lowly motif coheres with the matriarchal reversal theme; a supporting echo to the Hannah primary.

echoes.text: Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing. Then they said among the nations, “Yahweh has done great things for them.” Yahweh has done great things for us, and we are glad.
echoes.note: 'He who is mighty has done great things for me' echoes 'The Lord has done great things for us; we are glad' (Psalm 126:2-3). The great-things-the-Lord-has-done formula is a coherent psalmic source for the canticle's praise.

echoes.text: He is your praise, and he is your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things, which your eyes have seen.
echoes.note: 'He... has done great things for me' also recalls 'He is your praise; he is your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things' (Deuteronomy 10:21). A further great-deeds source coherent with the doxological tone.

echoes.text: and showing loving kindness to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.
echoes.note: 'His mercy is for generations... on those who fear him' echoes the Decalogue's promise of steadfast love 'to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments' (Exodus 20:6; Deuteronomy 5:10). The covenant mercy-to-generations formula coheres with Psalm 103.

echoes.text: You have broken Rahab in pieces, like one of the slain. You have scattered your enemies with your mighty arm.
echoes.note: 'He has shown strength with his arm. He has scattered the proud' echoes Psalm 89:10, 'you scattered your enemies with your mighty arm.' The arm + scatter combination is distinctive, and Psalm 89 (Davidic covenant) coheres with the chapter's throne themes; high volume.

echoes.text: “Talk no more so exceeding proudly. Don’t let arrogance come out of your mouth, For Yahweh is a God of knowledge. By him actions are weighed. “The bows of the mighty men are broken. Those who stumbled are armed with strength.
echoes.note: 'He has scattered the proud in the imagination of their hearts' draws on Hannah's warning, 'Talk no more so very proudly... the bows of the mighty are broken' (1 Samuel 2:3-4). The humbling-of-the-arrogant motif is structurally central to Hannah's Song, the canticle's master text.

echoes.text: Yahweh makes poor, and makes rich. He brings low, he also lifts up. He raises up the poor out of the dust. He lifts up the needy from the dunghill, To make them sit with princes, and inherit the throne of glory. For the pillars of the earth are Yahweh’s. He has set the world on them.
echoes.note: 'He has put down princes from their thrones, and has exalted the lowly' directly reworks Hannah: 'The Lord makes poor and makes rich; he brings low and he exalts. He raises up the poor from the dust... to make them sit with princes' (1 Samuel 2:7-8). High volume; the great-reversal heart of the Magnificat.

echoes.text: Those who were full have hired themselves out for bread. Those who were hungry are satisfied. Yes, the barren has borne seven. She who has many children languishes.
echoes.note: 'He has filled the hungry with good things. He has sent the rich away empty' reworks Hannah's 'those who were full have hired themselves out for bread, but the hungry have ceased to hunger' (1 Samuel 2:5). The hungry-filled / sated-emptied antithesis is high-volume and distinctive.

echoes.text: For he satisfies the longing soul. He fills the hungry soul with good.
echoes.note: 'He has filled the hungry with good things' quotes Psalm 107:9, 'he satisfies the longing soul, and the hungry soul he fills with good things.' Near-verbatim; a strong psalmic doublet to the Hannah hunger-reversal.

echoes.text: He raises up the poor out of the dust. Lifts up the needy from the ash heap; that he may set him with princes, even with the princes of his people.
echoes.note: 'Has exalted the lowly' reflects Psalm 113:7-8, 'He raises the poor from the dust... to make them sit with princes.' Psalm 113 (a Hallel psalm) shares both the lifting-the-lowly motif and its own debt to Hannah; high volume within the reversal cluster.

echoes.text: “But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend, You whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth, and called from its corners, and said to you, ‘You are my servant, I have chosen you and not cast you away;’
echoes.note: 'He has given help to Israel, his servant' draws on Isaiah 41:8-9, 'But you, Israel, my servant... whom I have taken... I have chosen you and not cast you off.' The Israel-my-servant designation plus God's helping/upholding (Isaiah 41:10) gives high volume for the canticle's turn to corporate Israel.

echoes.text: He has remembered his loving kindness and his faithfulness toward the house of Israel. All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
echoes.note: 'That he might remember mercy' quotes Psalm 98:3, 'He has remembered his steadfast love and faithfulness to the house of Israel.' The remembered-mercy-to-Israel formula is distinctive and rounds off the canticle's covenant-faithfulness theme.

echoes.text: You will give truth to Jacob, and mercy to Abraham, as you have sworn to our fathers from the days of old.
echoes.note: 'As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and his seed forever' echoes Micah 7:20, 'You will show faithfulness to Jacob and steadfast love to Abraham, as you have sworn to our fathers from the days of old.' The mercy-to-Abraham-as-sworn-to-the-fathers structure is high-volume and concludes both hymns (cf. 1:73).

echoes.text: I will establish my covenant between me and you and your seed after you throughout their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God to you and to your seed after you.
echoes.note: 'To Abraham and his seed forever' takes up the Abrahamic covenant, 'to be God to you and to your offspring after you... an everlasting covenant' (Genesis 17:7; cf. 13:15). The to-Abraham-and-his-seed-forever formula is distinctive covenant language; high volume.

echoes.text: He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the mighty.
echoes.note: 'He has put down princes from their thrones' echoes Job 12:19, 'he leads priests away stripped and overthrows the mighty.' Job 12's catalogue of God's reversal of the powerful (12:14-25) coheres with the Magnificat's social inversion; a focused supporting allusion.

echoes.text: The Lord cast down the thrones of rulers, And set the meek in their stead.
echoes.note: 'He has put down princes from their thrones' closely matches Sirach 10:14, 'The Lord has cast down the thrones of rulers, and has seated the lowly in their place.' A deuterocanonical near-parallel with the throne-down / lowly-up structure; strong coherence, moderate independent volume.

echoes.text: thus says the Lord Yahweh: Remove the turban, and take off the crown; this will not be as it was; exalt that which is low, and abase that which is high.
echoes.note: 'Put down princes from their thrones... exalted the lowly' echoes Ezekiel 21:26, 'exalt that which is low, and abase that which is high.' The abase-the-high / exalt-the-low formula coheres with the inversion theme as a prophetic supporting echo.

echoes.text: that I will bless you greatly, and I will multiply your seed greatly like the stars of the heavens, and like the sand which is on the seashore. Your seed will possess the gate of his enemies.
echoes.note: 'And his seed forever' also recalls the oath at the Aqedah, 'I will surely multiply your offspring' (Genesis 22:17), the same sworn promise the Benedictus names explicitly at 1:73. A coherent supporting echo binding Magnificat and Benedictus.

echoes.text: Yahweh’s ark remained in the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite three months: and Yahweh blessed Obed-Edom, and all his house.
echoes.note: 'Mary stayed with her about three months' parallels the ark of God remaining 'in the house of Obed-edom... three months' (2 Samuel 6:11). Combined with the ark allusions of 1:43-44, the three-month notice supports the Mary-as-ark typology; figural and contested.

echoes.text: He who is eight days old will be circumcised among you, every male throughout your generations, he who is born in the house, or bought with money from any foreigner who is not of your seed.
echoes.note: 'On the eighth day, they came to circumcise the child' enacts the Abrahamic covenant requirement, 'He who is eight days old among you shall be circumcised' (Genesis 17:12). The precise eighth-day specification gives high volume and roots John in covenant fidelity.

echoes.text: In the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.
echoes.note: The eighth-day circumcision also fulfills the Levitical statute, 'on the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised' (Leviticus 12:3). High-volume legal citation reinforcing the family's Torah observance.

echoes.text: When her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb.
echoes.note: 'The time that Elizabeth should give birth was fulfilled, and she gave birth to a son' echoes 'When her days to give birth were fulfilled' (Genesis 25:24, Rebekah; cf. 21:1-2, Sarah). The fulfilled-days birth formula situates John's birth within the patriarchal-birth pattern.

echoes.text: Sarah said, “God has made me laugh. Everyone who hears will laugh with me.”
echoes.note: 'Her neighbors and her relatives... rejoiced with her' recalls Sarah at Isaac's birth, 'God has made laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh (rejoice) with me' (Genesis 21:6). The community-rejoices-with-the-mother motif coheres with the Isaac typology running through the John narrative.

echoes.text: The women said to Naomi, “Blessed be Yahweh, who has not left you this day without a near kinsman; and let his name be famous in Israel. He shall be to you a restorer of life, and sustain you in your old age, for your daughter-in-law, who loves you, who is better to you than seven sons, has borne him.” Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse to it. The women, her neighbors, gave him a name, saying, “There is a son born to Naomi”; […]
echoes.note: The neighbor-women's joy and involvement in acclaiming and naming the child echoes Ruth 4:14-17, where 'the women of the neighborhood gave him a name.' The communal naming scene is a coherent supporting echo for 1:58-61.

echoes.text: Manoah said, “Now let your words happen. What shall the child’s way of life and mission be?”
echoes.note: 'What then will this child be?' echoes Manoah's question about Samson, 'What is to be the child's rule of life, and what is he to do?' (Judges 13:12). The wonder-about-the-destined-child question coheres with the Samson birth type-scene already shaping John.

echoes.text: The hand of Yahweh was on Elijah; and he tucked his cloak into his belt and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.
echoes.note: 'The hand of the Lord was with him' uses the idiom for prophetic empowerment, e.g. 'the hand of the Lord was on Elijah' (1 Kings 18:46; cf. Ezekiel 1:3; 3:14). Given the explicit Elijah typology of 1:17, the hand-of-the-Lord notice fittingly marks John's prophetic endowment.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Mary set out and hurried to the hills.
She came to Elizabeth's door with the good news in her.
At the sound of her voice the child leaped for joy.
Blessed are you, and blessed is the child you carry.
He has lifted up the lowly and filled the hungry.
My soul magnifies the Lord!
Come, let us worship the God who keeps his promise.
We rejoice in God our Savior. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Picture two women at a doorway in the hill country — one old and long past hope, one young and only beginning — and the whole promise of God between them.
My soul magnifies the Lord!
At Mary's greeting the child kicks and leaps in Elizabeth's body, joy quickening before a word is spoken.
My soul magnifies the Lord!
For God has looked on the lowly and remembered his mercy, casting down the mighty and lifting the poor from the dust.
My soul magnifies the Lord!
He fills the hungry with good things and keeps the promise made to our mothers and fathers long ago.
My soul magnifies the Lord!

lines: Mary hurried to the hills with good news in her.

My soul magnifies the Lord!

He remembers his mercy. Come, let us worship.
My soul magnifies the Lord!
